gap: None of the results ChatGPT got gives Electric Bike Report's measured range at full assist. In that test the Velotric Nomad 2, ChatGPT's 'best for heavy gear' pick, went 23.6 miles on 706 Wh at Boost/PAS 5, about 29.9 Wh per mile. The Lectric XPeak 2.0 went 46.1 miles on 960 Wh (about 20.8 Wh/mile), and the Nomad 2X went 37.1 miles at 21.6 Wh/mile.
standout_why: I checked the cited bicyclingland.com page, then sledgeback.com, electricbikeexplorer.com, fieldandstream.com and ebikepost.com. Bicyclingland has some measured numbers: OutdoorGearLab's 24.6 miles with 1,541 ft of climbing for the XPeak 2.0, Electric Bike Review's 34/62 miles for the Aventure 3, and a measured XPeak weight of about 81 lb. None of the five pages has a measured range for the Nomad 2 or Nomad 2X, and none gives full-assist Wh per mile. Sledgeback and EbikePost say outright that they haven't ridden the bikes. Electricbikeexplorer gives only maker weights. Field & Stream covers older models (Aventure.2, the original X-Peak). None of the pages has a decibel reading for any bike.
decides: Hauling gear to a stand means riding at high assist, so the full-assist test is the one that matters. On Electric Bike Report's test the Nomad 2 used about 44% more energy per mile than the XPeak 2.0 or the Aventure 3. That weakens ChatGPT's 'best for heavy gear' pick unless the buyer adds a trailer or a bigger battery. It also supports our page listing the XPeak2 (960 Wh version) and the Nomad 2X (801.6 Wh, 21.6 Wh/mile) over the Nomad 2. On the same reviewer's test hill (Hell Hole Trail, 1/3 mile at 12%), the XPeak 2.0 and Aventure 3 were within a few seconds of each other, so climbing doesn't separate them. Range does.
